texts.preamble: Pankaj Pednekar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through A.B. ... on 17 December, 2018 -1- High Court Of Madhya Pradesh, Bench At Indore Crr No.5780/2018 Pankaj Pednekar s/o Dr.Kailash Pednekar vs. State of M.P 17.12.2018 (Indore):
texts.facts: Apart from the hearing on admission, learned Senior Counsel for the applicant also made submissions on IA No.8489/18, which is an application for suspension of sentence. Put briefly, the case of the prosecution is that on 19.10.2004 at around 11.00 A.M an inspection was carried out by Food Inspector at the shop of applicant situated at Freeganj, Ujjain, where sealed packets of milk biscuits were kept for being sold. The Food Inspector purchased the milk biscuits and adopting due procedure, the sample of the biscuits were sent to Public Analyst, State Food Laboratory for examination. On examination it was found that the biscuits were misbranded as there was no mention of manufacutring date and batch number. On the basis of the report of the Public Analyst, the applicant was charge sheeted under sections 16(1)(a)(i) & 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
texts.arguments: During arguments, learned Senior Counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant has already suffered imprisonment since 26.11.2018 and has faced prosecution for 13 years and looking to his detention in jail as already suffered by him to be considered appropriate sentence and in that case he would not be inclined to press IA No.8489/18 for suspension of sentence. Considered. This apart, learned counsel for the applicant made an admission on behalf of the applicant that he did not possess the requisite license for selling the packets of biscuits which were seized.
texts.petitioner_arguments: During arguments, learned Senior Counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant has already suffered imprisonment since 26.11.2018 and has faced prosecution for 13 years and looking to his detention in jail as already suffered by him to be considered appropriate sentence and in that case he would not be inclined to press IA No.8489/18 for suspension of sentence. Considered. This apart, learned counsel for the applicant made an admission on behalf of the applicant that he did not possess the requisite license for selling the packets of biscuits which were seized.
